category: PCB panel modes, object classes, Design/Tools menu commands & Layer Stack Manager features
description: The editing modes of the PCB panel, the object class types managed by Design > Classes, additional Design/Tools/Edit menu commands of the PCB editor not covered elsewhere, and the tabs and features of the Layer Stack Manager (impedance profiles, via types, back drills, material library, presets).

tools.name: PCB panel > Nets mode
tools.description: Lists net classes, their nets and each net's primitives with routed length, pin count and the routing status; selecting entries highlights them using Normal / Mask / Dim modes with optional Select, Zoom and Clear Existing. Right-click offers net colour, Change Net Color, source/terminator pad assignment for topology, Un-Route Net, and net-class editing.
tools.usage: View > Panels > PCB, mode drop-down = Nets

parameters.name: Normal / Mask / Dim
parameters.description: Highlight style for selected items.

parameters.name: Select / Zoom / Clear Existing
parameters.description: Whether entries are selected, zoomed to and previous highlights cleared.

tools.example: Choose Nets mode, click class 'DDR', tick Zoom and Mask to isolate the DDR routing on screen.
tools.notes: Net colour overrides set here are drawn according to PCB Editor > Board Insight Color Overrides.

tools.name: PCB panel > Components mode
tools.description: Browses component classes, components and each component's primitives (pads, strings, bodies); supports selection, zoom, masking and quick property edits via double-click. Useful for stepping through placement by class or locating parts by designator.
tools.usage: View > Panels > PCB, mode = Components
tools.example: Components mode, class 'Sheet_PSU', Select + Zoom: all power-supply parts are selected for Tools > Component Placement > Arrange Within Rectangle.
tools.notes: Component classes come from Class Generation options in Project Options.

tools.name: PCB panel > Differential Pairs Editor mode
tools.description: Creates and edits differential pairs and pair classes on the PCB: Add (pick positive/negative nets), Create From Nets (by _P/_N or custom suffix filters), Delete, and Rule Wizard to generate Differential Pairs Routing rules for the selected pair/class. Shows pair length, uncoupled length and routing status.
tools.usage: View > Panels > PCB, mode = Differential Pairs Editor

parameters.name: Create From Nets
parameters.description: Filter by net name pattern with positive/negative suffixes.

parameters.name: Rule Wizard
parameters.description: Generates Width/Gap/Clearance rules for the pairs.

tools.example: Differential Pairs Editor > Create From Nets, filter 'USB*', +suffix _P, -suffix _N, create pairs; then Rule Wizard to add the routing rule.
tools.notes: Pairs defined on the schematic with Differential Pair directives arrive through the ECO automatically.

tools.name: PCB panel > Polygons mode
tools.description: Lists polygon classes and polygon pours with net, layer, pour status (poured/shelved/modified) and area; supports select/zoom/mask, repour and shelve commands from the right-click menu and drag-and-drop pour ordering. Complements the Polygon Manager dialog.
tools.usage: View > Panels > PCB, mode = Polygons
tools.example: Polygons mode, right-click a stale pour > Repour, or select several and choose Shelve.
tools.notes: Pour order (which polygon pours first) is edited in Polygon Manager > Pour Order or by dragging here.

tools.name: PCB panel > Hole Size Editor mode
tools.description: Tabulates all pad/via holes grouped by size, plated state and shape (round/slot/square), with counts; selecting a group highlights every hole of that size so unintended drill sizes can be consolidated. Columns include Hole Size, Hole Type, Plated, Count and Layer Pair.
tools.usage: View > Panels > PCB, mode = Hole Size Editor
tools.example: Sort by Count, find a lone 0.31 mm hole, select it and change Hole Size to 0.3 mm in Properties to reduce the drill table.
tools.notes: The Drill Table in Draftsman / drill drawing mirrors this grouping.

tools.name: PCB panel > 3D Models mode
tools.description: Lists components with their 3D bodies, model type (STEP/Parasolid, extruded, cylinder, sphere), height and colour/opacity, allowing per-model visibility, opacity and colour overrides and quick location of components lacking 3D bodies.
tools.usage: View > Panels > PCB, mode = 3D Models
tools.example: Filter for components with no body, then use Tools > Manage 3D Bodies for Components on Board to assign models.
tools.notes: Model search paths are set in PCB Editor > Models.

tools.name: PCB panel > Structure Classes mode
tools.description: Browses structure classes: hierarchical classes generated from the schematic sheet structure (one per sheet symbol, containing its component and net classes), used for rule scoping with InStructureClass and for selecting everything belonging to a subsystem.
tools.usage: View > Panels > PCB, mode = Structure Classes (requires Project Options > Class Generation > structure classes)
tools.example: Select structure class 'Audio', Select + Zoom to grab all audio nets and parts for a room.
tools.notes: Comparator/ECO options must include Structure Classes for them to be transferred.

tools.name: PCB panel > Unions mode
tools.description: Lists unions (groups of components/primitives that move together) and their members; unions are created with Tools > Convert > Create Union from selected objects and broken with Break Union. Selecting a union selects all its members.
tools.usage: View > Panels > PCB, mode = Unions
tools.example: Create a union from a filter block (inductor, caps, silkscreen), then drag the union as one and copy it with Copy Room Formats-style placement across channels.
tools.notes: Query keywords InUnion(n) / InNamedUnion('name').

tools.name: PCB panel > From-To Editor / Split Plane Editor / Layer Stack Regions / Pad & Via Templates / xSignals modes
tools.description: Remaining PCB panel modes: From-To Editor (define pad-to-pad connections for custom topologies), Split Plane Editor (view plane layers and assign nets to split regions), Layer Stack Regions (assign sub-stacks to board regions in rigid-flex), Pad & Via Templates (browse/apply templates from local or Pad Via Libraries) and xSignals (create/manage xSignals and classes with length/status columns).
tools.usage: View > Panels > PCB, mode drop-down
tools.example: Split Plane Editor: pick Internal Plane 1, select a split region, right-click > Properties to assign net GND.
tools.notes: The mode list depends on features enabled in the Layer Stack Manager (e.g. Layer Stack Regions needs rigid-flex).

tools.name: Design > Classes > Net Classes
tools.description: Object Class Explorer section for net classes: create classes, move nets between Non-Members and Members, and rename. Net classes are the main scoping handle for Width/Clearance/Via rules and are normally generated from the schematic (buses, net class directives, harnesses) with manual additions allowed on the PCB (which the comparator can be told to keep).
tools.usage: Design > Classes > Net Classes (Object Class Explorer)

parameters.name: Members / Non-Members
parameters.description: Nets in and out of the class.

tools.example: Add class 'HV' with nets AC_L, AC_N; then create a Clearance rule InNetClass('HV') to All 3 mm.
tools.notes: Project Options > Comparator > Extra Net Classes controls whether PCB-only classes are removed on the next ECO.

tools.name: Design > Classes > Component Classes
tools.description: Manage component classes (groups of designators) for placement rules, mask rules, panel browsing and the Arrange Within Room commands. Sheet-based classes are generated automatically when Project Options > Class Generation > Component Classes is enabled.
tools.usage: Design > Classes > Component Classes
tools.example: Create class 'TallParts' with electrolytics and connectors; Height rule InComponentClass('TallParts') Max 20 mm; Permitted Layers Top only.
tools.notes: Query keyword InComponentClass.

tools.name: Design > Classes > Layer Classes
tools.description: Groups of layers (e.g. Outer Layers, Inner Signal, Planes) that can be used in rule scopes with InLayerClass / ComponentInLayerClass, so one Width or Clearance rule can apply to a set of layers without listing each name.
tools.usage: Design > Classes > Layer Classes
tools.example: Class 'InnerSignal' = Mid Layer 1..4; Width rule InLayerClass('InnerSignal') Preferred 0.1 mm.
tools.notes: Default classes All Layers, Electrical Layers, Signal Layers, Component Layers exist automatically.

tools.name: Design > Classes > Pad Classes / Polygon Classes / From-To Classes
tools.description: Pad Classes group individual pads (across components) for mask or clearance rules (InPadClass); Polygon Classes group pours for connect-style rules and pour ordering (InPolygonClass); From-To Classes group custom from-to connections for topology/length rules (InFromToClass).
tools.usage: Design > Classes > Pad Classes | Polygon Classes | From-To Classes
tools.example: Pad class 'ThermalPads' containing U1-33, U2-EP; Paste Mask Expansion rule InPadClass('ThermalPads') -25%.
tools.notes: Pad classes must be maintained on the PCB; they are not derived from the schematic.

tools.name: Design > Classes > Differential Pair Classes / xSignal Classes / Design Channel Classes / Structure Classes
tools.description: Class kinds for high-speed and hierarchical scoping: Differential Pair Classes (InDifferentialPairClass), xSignal Classes (InxSignalClass, created by the xSignal wizard), Design Channel Classes (one per multi-channel instance, InChannelClass) and Structure Classes (hierarchy, InStructureClass). All appear in the Object Class Explorer with member editing.
tools.usage: Design > Classes > Differential Pair Classes | xSignal Classes | Design Channel Classes | Structure Classes
tools.example: xSignal class 'DDR3_DQ' built by the wizard; Matched Lengths rule InxSignalClass('DDR3_DQ') 0.5 mm.
tools.notes: Channel classes are generated by the multi-channel compiler; do not edit them manually.

tools.name: Design > xSignals > Run xSignal Wizard / Create xSignals
tools.description: Sub-menu for extended signals: Run xSignal Wizard (select source component, target components and series terminators to generate xSignals and classes for DDR/PCIe-style buses), Create xSignals Between Components and Create xSignals From Connections; xSignals are then managed in the PCB panel's xSignals mode.
tools.usage: Design > xSignals > Run xSignal Wizard | Create xSignals Between Components | Create xSignals From Connections

parameters.name: Source / Target components
parameters.description: Endpoints between which xSignals are created.

parameters.name: xSignal class name
parameters.description: Class to collect the generated xSignals.

tools.example: Run xSignal Wizard > On-board DDR3/DDR4 preset > pick U1 (controller) and U2/U3 (DRAMs) > creates DQ/DQS/ADDR xSignal classes with matched-length rules.
tools.notes: xSignals let length rules span series resistors/capacitors; verify results in the PCB panel xSignals mode.

tools.name: Design > Board Shape submenu
tools.description: Board outline commands: Define Board Shape from Selected Objects, Define Board Shape from 3D Body, Create Primitives From Board Shape, Define Board Cutout From Selected Objects (selected regions become cutouts), and, in Board Planning Mode, Redefine Board Shape, Edit Board Shape and the split-line tools for dividing the board into regions (View > Board Planning Mode).
tools.usage: Design > Board Shape > Define Board Shape from Selected Objects | Define from 3D body | Create Primitives from Board Shape | Define Board Cutout from Selected Objects; View > Board Planning Mode
tools.example: Import the outline DXF onto Mechanical 1, select its lines/arcs, Design > Board Shape > Define Board Shape from Selected Objects.
tools.notes: Board shape edges are what Board Outline Clearance measures; export the shape as Gerber via Create Primitives on a mechanical layer.

tools.name: Design > Make PCB Library / Make Integrated Library (from PCB)
tools.description: Make PCB Library collects every footprint used on the board into a new .PcbLib (project library) for archiving or editing; Make Integrated Library builds an .IntLib of the symbols and models used by the project. Both are the standard way to snapshot the exact library content a released design used.
tools.usage: Design > Make PCB Library (PCB editor); Design > Make Integrated Library (schematic editor)
tools.example: Before release: Design > Make PCB Library, save 'Board_Footprints.PcbLib' into the project folder and add it to the project.
tools.notes: Schematic-side counterpart: Design > Make Schematic Library.

tools.name: Tools > Testpoint Manager
tools.description: Dialog that assigns, clears and reports fabrication and assembly test points according to the Testpoint Style and Usage rules: Assign All / Assign for nets without test points, Clear All, per-net status, side and whether existing pads/vias were reused or new ones must be added. Feeds the Test Point Report and the IPC-D-356 netlist.
tools.usage: Tools > Testpoint Manager (tabs Fabrication / Assembly)

parameters.name: Assign All Test Points
parameters.description: Auto-assign according to rules.

parameters.name: Clear All Test Points
parameters.description: Remove assignments.

tools.example: Set Fabrication Testpoint Usage Required for All, Style rule size 1 mm bottom side, then Tools > Testpoint Manager > Assign All Test Points; review nets marked 'No suitable pad'.
tools.notes: Pads/vias flagged as test points show a testpoint marker and carry Fabrication/Assembly testpoint flags in the Testpoint section of their Properties panel.

tools.name: Tools > Pin/Part Swapping
tools.description: Sub-menu for logical swapping: Configure (enable pin and part swapping per component and define swap groups, or take them from the schematic/FPGA pin file), Interactive Pin/Net Swapping (click two pins to exchange their nets), Interactive Part Swapping (swap equivalent parts such as gates), Automatic Net/Pin Optimizer (minimise crossings). Swaps must be pushed back with Design > Update Schematics.
tools.usage: Tools > Pin/Part Swapping > Configure... | Interactive Pin/Net Swapping | Interactive Part Swapping | Automatic Net/Pin Optimizer

parameters.name: Swap groups
parameters.description: Pins/parts allowed to interchange (Component Properties > Pin Swapping).

tools.example: Configure U1 (FPGA) pins in bank groups, then Automatic Net/Pin Optimizer on the connector nets; ECO to schematic.
tools.notes: Pin swap data can also be defined in the schematic symbol (Pin Properties > Pin/Part Swapping).

tools.name: Tools > Re-Annotate (positional re-annotation)
tools.description: Renumbers component designators on the PCB according to physical position (X then Y ascending/descending, by side, with start index and suffix options), producing a .WAS/.IS change file; the new designators are pushed to the schematic with Design > Update Schematics (or Back Annotate in the schematic editor).
tools.usage: Tools > Re-Annotate...

parameters.name: Positional order
parameters.description: 1: X ascending then Y, 2: Y then X, etc. (five schemes).

parameters.name: Start index / Locked designators
parameters.description: Numbering start and exclusions.

tools.example: Tools > Re-Annotate, choose scheme '1 By Ascending X Then Ascending Y', OK, then Design > Update Schematics to sync.
tools.notes: Board Level Annotation in the schematic editor is the alternative for multi-channel designs.

tools.name: Tools > Component Placement > Place From File / Position Component / Auto Placement
tools.description: Placement helpers: Place From File imports a pick-and-place style CSV/text of designator, X, Y, rotation, layer to position parts; Position Component asks for exact coordinates for a chosen part; Arrange Within Room / Rectangle / Outside Board and Reposition Selected Components cluster parts; legacy Auto Placement (Cluster/Statistical placers) may exist as Legacy Tools.
tools.usage: Tools > Component Placement > Place From File... | Position Component | Arrange Within Room | Arrange Within Rectangle | Arrange Outside Board | Reposition Selected Components

parameters.name: Placement file
parameters.description: Designator, Mid X, Mid Y, Rotation, Layer columns (header line required).

tools.example: Export Pick and Place from the golden board, edit coordinates in Excel, Tools > Component Placement > Place From File on the new board revision.
tools.notes: Units are read from the file header or the dialog; check origin (absolute vs relative).

tools.name: Tools > Remove Unused Pad Shapes
tools.description: Deletes the copper of multilayer pads and vias on internal layers where they have no connection, reducing capacitance and improving routing space (non-functional pad removal). Options: apply to pads and/or vias, selected objects only, and preserve outer layers; results are reversible with Restore Unused Pad Shapes.
tools.usage: Tools > Remove Unused Pad Shapes... (Restore Unused Pad Shapes to revert)

parameters.name: Pads / Vias
parameters.description: Object kinds to process.

parameters.name: Selected objects only
parameters.description: Limit to the selection.

tools.example: Run on all vias before Gerber output; the Gerber inner layers then show anti-pads only where the via passes without connection.
tools.notes: Some fabricators prefer to do this themselves; confirm before enabling.

tools.name: Tools > Manage 3D Bodies for Components on Board
tools.description: Dialog listing every footprint on the board with its current 3D body status, allowing extruded bodies to be generated from footprint outlines (with height/layer), STEP models assigned by search or path, and bodies updated across all instances of a footprint at once.
tools.usage: Tools > Manage 3D Bodies for Components on Board

parameters.name: Body state
parameters.description: Add extruded body / assign model / leave.

parameters.name: Height / Layer
parameters.description: For generated extruded bodies.

tools.example: Filter rows with no body, set Body State = Add Extruded, height from the 'Height' parameter, Close: the 3D view now shows placeholder blocks for every part.
tools.notes: Bodies created here live on the board only; update the library to make them permanent.

tools.name: Tools > Convert > Create Union / Break Union / Create Board Region from Selected Primitives
tools.description: Conversion commands beyond track/polygon conversion: Create Union from selected objects (move as a group), Break Union, Convert Selected Tracks to Polygon, Convert Selected Primitives to Component/Free Primitives, Create Board Region from Selected Primitives (for rigid-flex sub-stack regions), Explode Component to Free Primitives, Create Region from Selected Primitives, Create Cutout From Selected Primitives.
tools.usage: Tools > Convert > Create Union from selected objects | Break Union | Create Region from Selected Primitives | Create Cutout From Selected Primitives | Convert Selected Tracks To Polygon | Explode Component to Free Primitives
tools.example: Select the closed track outline of a copper pad shape, Tools > Convert > Create Region from Selected Primitives, then assign it to the pad's net.
tools.notes: Exploding components is destructive for ECO synchronisation; prefer editing the footprint in the library.

tools.name: Layer Stack Manager > Stackup tab
tools.description: Grid of layers (Signal, Plane, Dielectric Core/Prepreg, Solder Mask, Overlay, Surface Finish, plus Coverlay/Stiffener/Adhesive in flex mode) with columns Name, Material, Type, Weight/Thickness, Dk, Df, Pullback and Orientation; Add/Delete layers via right-click or the Add menu, materials come from the Material Library, and the Properties panel gives Board-level options (Stack Symmetry, Library Compliance) and per-layer details. The stack drives impedance, 3D thickness, Gerber layer lists and the Board Stack Report.
tools.usage: Design > Layer Stack Manager > Stackup tab

parameters.name: Layer Type
parameters.description: Signal | Plane | Dielectric (Core/Prepreg) | Solder Mask | Overlay | Surface Finish | Coverlay | Stiffener.

parameters.name: Material / Thickness / Dk / Df
parameters.description: Material properties used by the impedance calculator.

tools.example: Tools > Presets > 6 layer, then replace each dielectric with an FR-4 material from Tools > Material Library and set copper to 1 oz.
tools.notes: Save the stack as a preset or template for reuse; Tools > Layerstack Visualizer shows a 3D cross-section.

tools.name: Layer Stack Manager > Impedance tab (impedance profiles)
tools.description: Defines named impedance profiles: Type (Single, Differential, Single-Coplanar, Differential-Coplanar), Target Impedance and Tolerance; the field-solver (Simberian-based) calculates Width (and Gap) per signal layer against the stack's reference planes, shown in the profile grid. Width / Differential Pairs Routing rules can reference a profile (Use Impedance Profile) so routing widths follow the stack.
tools.usage: Design > Layer Stack Manager > Impedance tab > Add Impedance Profile; Properties panel for Type/Target/Tolerance

parameters.name: Type
parameters.description: Single | Differential | Single-Coplanar | Differential-Coplanar.

parameters.name: Reference layers
parameters.description: Top/Bottom reference selection per signal layer.

tools.example: Add profile 'DIFF90' Differential 90 ohm; on Top Layer it computes W 0.16 mm / G 0.18 mm; create a Differential Pairs Routing rule using profile DIFF90 for InDifferentialPairClass('USB').
tools.notes: Results depend on the material Dk values; coplanar types also need the Clearance rule to keep pour distance consistent.

tools.name: Layer Stack Manager > Via Types tab
tools.description: Defines the allowed via spans (drill pairs): Name, First Layer, Last Layer, Type (Thru, Blind, Buried), uVia flag (laser microvia) and Mirror (create the mirrored span automatically). Only spans defined here can be used by Place > Via, routing layer changes (6 / 8 keys) and the Routing Via Style rule; the Layer Pairs rule enforces them.
tools.usage: Design > Layer Stack Manager > Via Types tab > Add

parameters.name: First Layer / Last Layer
parameters.description: Span of the via.

parameters.name: uVia / Mirror
parameters.description: Microvia flag; auto-create the symmetric span.

tools.example: Add 'uVia_L1-L2' Top Layer to Mid Layer 1 with uVia and Mirror, giving the Bottom-L(n-1) counterpart for a 1+N+1 HDI stack.
tools.notes: Tab is unavailable for single-copper-layer stacks; stacked/skip microvia allowances interact with Hole To Hole Clearance.

tools.name: Layer Stack Manager > Back Drills tab
tools.description: Enabled through Features > Back Drills: defines back-drill pairs (drilling side, target layer/depth) that remove unused via stubs. The Max Via Stub Length rule identifies which vias qualify; NC Drill output then emits separate back-drill files and the Drill Table lists them.
tools.usage: Design > Layer Stack Manager > Features > Back Drills, then Back Drills tab > Add

parameters.name: Drill from / To layer
parameters.description: Side and depth of the back drill.

tools.example: Add back drill from Bottom Layer to Mid Layer 6; set rule Max Via Stub Length 0.25 mm on the SERDES class; run DRC and check BackDrillBottom in the PCB Filter.
tools.notes: Back drills appear on the drill drawing with distinct symbols.

tools.name: Layer Stack Manager > Features and Tools menus (Rigid/Flex, Printed Electronics, Material Library, Presets, Layerstack Visualizer)
tools.description: Features enables optional modes: Rigid/Flex (standard, one flex sub-stack), Rigid/Flex (Advanced, multiple sub-stacks and the Board tab), Back Drills and Printed Electronics (additive layer stacks). Tools offers Material Library (manage dielectric/copper/mask materials and their Dk/Df), Presets (2-16 layer templates), Measurement Units, Layerstack Visualizer (3D cross-section) and Library Compliance checks. The Board tab (advanced rigid-flex) creates and edits sub-stacks.
tools.usage: Design > Layer Stack Manager > Features > Rigid/Flex | Rigid/Flex (Advanced) | Back Drills | Printed Electronics; Tools > Material Library | Presets | Layerstack Visualizer
tools.example: Features > Rigid/Flex (Advanced), Board tab > Add Substack 'Flex' (polyimide core + coverlay), then assign it to a region in Board Planning Mode.
tools.notes: Single-copper-layer stacks disable Via Types and Back Drills; File > Save saves the stack into the PcbDoc.

tools.name: Material Library (Layer Stack Manager)
tools.description: Catalogue of stackup materials grouped by type (Core, Prepreg, Copper, Solder Mask, Surface Finish, Coverlay, Adhesive, Stiffener) with manufacturer, thickness, Dk/Df (frequency dependent) and process data; materials are dragged onto stack layers so impedance calculations use real vendor values. Custom materials can be added and shared through Workspace templates.
tools.usage: Design > Layer Stack Manager > Tools > Material Library

parameters.name: Type / Manufacturer / Thickness / Dk / Df
parameters.description: Material properties.

tools.example: Add Isola 370HR 0.1 mm core (Dk 4.04 @1 GHz), select it for Dielectric 2, and re-check the DIFF90 profile widths.
tools.notes: Library Compliance in Board properties flags layers using materials not in the library.

tools.name: Design > Board Options > Objects Snap / Snap Options
tools.description: Board Options (Properties panel with nothing selected) hold the snapping controls: Snap To Grids, Snap To Guides, Snap To Object Axis (extend lines from object edges) and Snap To Object Hotspots (pad/via centres, track ends) with Snap Distance and range, plus Snap to Linear Guides/Point Guides and Axis snapping on/off per object kind. Ctrl+E pops up the same choices during editing.
tools.usage: Design > Board Options... (Properties panel > Snap Options); Ctrl+E during a command

parameters.name: Snap To Object Hotspots
parameters.description: Snap range and object kinds (pads, vias, tracks, arcs, regions, texts...).

parameters.name: Snap To Object Axis
parameters.description: Enable axis-alignment guides with range.

tools.example: Disable Snap To Grids and enable Object Hotspots 'Pads' only to route exactly to pad centres regardless of grid.
tools.notes: Grid Manager and Guide Manager live on the same Board Options page.

tools.name: Design > Board Layers & Colors (View Configuration: View Options / 3D settings)
tools.description: The View Configuration panel's second tab, View Options, holds general settings (Configuration name, Signal Layer/Overlay visibility toggles), 3D settings (Board thickness, Colours by Layer/Realistic, opacity per layer, Show 3D bodies, Show Solder Mask), Mask and Dim levels, Object Visibility (per object kind draft/final, transparency), and Additional Options (pad/via nets, test points, dimension units, origin marker, status info). Layer colours and enable flags are on the Layers & Colors tab (L).
tools.usage: L or Design > Board Layers & Colors... > View Options tab

parameters.name: Mask Level / Dim Level
parameters.description: Contrast for masked/dimmed objects.

parameters.name: 3D: Colors by layer / Realistic, Board thickness, Show solder mask
parameters.description: 3D rendering options.

tools.example: View Options > 3D > Colors by layer, Board thickness from stack; set Top Solder opacity to 30% to inspect copper under mask in 3D.
tools.notes: Configurations (layer/colour sets) are saved with the document and selectable at the top of the panel.

tools.name: Reports > Board Information / Measure Selected Objects / Netlist Status
tools.description: Reports menu items of the PCB editor beyond BOM: Board Information (summary of counts, board dimensions, layers, drill pairs, DRC violations; Report button writes HTML/TXT), Measure Distance (Ctrl+M), Measure Primitives (edge-to-edge between two primitives), Measure Selected Objects (total length of selected tracks/arcs), Netlist Status (routed length and status per net), Project Reports (Design Hierarchy, BOM, Cross Reference) and Layer Stack Report.
tools.usage: Reports > Board Information | Measure Distance | Measure Primitives | Measure Selected Objects | Netlist Status | Layer Stack Report | Project Reports
tools.example: Select all segments of net CLK, Reports > Measure Selected Objects to read the total routed length including arcs.
tools.notes: Report generation can be disabled/enabled per report in Preferences > PCB Editor > Reports.

tools.name: Place > Dimension types (Linear, Angular, Radial, Leader, Datum, Baseline, Center, Linear Diameter, Radial Diameter, Standard)
tools.description: PCB dimension objects placed on mechanical/documentation layers: Linear (point-to-point with extension lines), Angular (between two lines), Radial (arc radius), Leader (arrow with text), Datum (running dimensions from a datum), Baseline (stacked from a common base), Center (crosshair at an arc centre), Linear Diameter and Radial Diameter (circles/holes), and the legacy Standard dimension. Properties: units, precision, arrow style/size, text height, prefix/suffix, layer.
tools.usage: Place > Dimension > Linear | Angular | Radial | Leader | Datum | Baseline | Center | Linear Diameter | Radial Diameter | Standard

parameters.name: Unit / Precision / Format
parameters.description: mm/mil/inch, decimals, text prefix/suffix.

parameters.name: Layer
parameters.description: Usually a mechanical documentation layer.

tools.example: Place > Dimension > Linear on Mechanical 4 between the two mounting holes; set precision 2 and unit mm in Properties.
tools.notes: For production drawings prefer Draftsman dimensions, which update automatically and support GD&T.

tools.name: Place > Keepout submenu and layer-specific keepouts
tools.description: Keepout objects (Track, Arc, Fill, Region) placed via Place > Keepout on the Keep-Out Layer (all layers) or drawn on a specific copper layer with the Keepout attribute set in Properties, with per-object restrictions on what they block (Copper, Vias, Component bodies, Tracks, Pads, SMD Pads, Component). Interactive routing, autorouting, polygon pours and DRC obey them; keepouts are excluded from outputs.
tools.usage: Place > Keepout > Track | Arc | Fill | Region; or place a primitive and enable Keepout with Restrictions in Properties

parameters.name: Restrictions
parameters.description: Copper | Via | Component | Track | Pad | SMD Pad | Component body.

tools.example: Place > Keepout > Region around an antenna area on Top Layer restricting Copper and Components; the GND pour now avoids it.
tools.notes: Board-edge clearance is better handled with the Board Outline Clearance rule than with keepouts.
